names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 21 Ιουνίου, «Οσία Αναστασία της Σερβίας», with the rank word left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 21. јун ст. ст., „Преподобна Анастасија, мајка Светог Саве“ — Преподобна is the rank and comes off, and „мајка Светог Саве“ is a description of her and not part of her name, so it comes off too; §6 would keep it out in any case, naming another saint inside a stored form being the thing that rule exists to stop. The bare name is what is left. Her baptismal «Ана», which the body gives, is **measured and not written**: one form per folder, the fullest, and the monastic name is the one the heading gives. **The fold is deliberate and forced**: `foldchk.py` returns `anastasia-of-rome-15-april` and `anastasia-the-patrician`, both `sr`, for «Анастасија», so this is the third folder on the string, and the heading has nothing to break it with. A `READ_FOLDS` key is added for it in the same commit.

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 21 Ιουνίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing, and gives no year at all. The whole of what it says of her is that she was the mother of Sava, whom it sends the reader to find on 14 Ιανουαρίου — the day the corpus's `sava-of-serbia` already carries on its Greek row — and that no other details of her life are known. She is none of the corpus's seven other Anastasias, all of whom are Roman, Serbian-unrelated or twentieth-century. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 04.07.2026 (21. јун ст. ст.) — „Преподобна Анастасија, мајка Светог Саве“

attestations.note: The day’s fifth entry, and **the folder of this wave that gained the most from one entry**, its only other book having printed a sentence and a disclaimer. The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, without a closing full stop, as every heading of this wave is. The Julian 21 June is the same menologion number this folder’s other venerated rows carry, so there is no second day and no §4 note is owed. **A FIRST DATE ON A FOLDER THAT HELD `dates: null`, AND IT IS STATED OF THE DEATH.** saint.gr’s whole account is «Η Οσία Αναστασία της Σερβίας ήταν η μητέρα του Οσίου Σάββα» followed by «Δεν έχουμε άλλες λεπτομέρειες» — no century, no place beyond Serbia in her title, no year of any kind. This book: „Упокојила се 21. јуна 1200. године“, she reposed on 21 June 1200. `death` 1200 to 1200, display «1200», basis traditional. **The day in that sentence is the day of the feast**, which is the one place in this wave where the source’s own year of death carries the menologion number the row is written on, and the agreement is recorded rather than used: the feast comes off `sr-cand.mjs`’s first line as it always does. **1196 IS REFUSED AND IT IS NOT A BIRTH.** „Замонашила се 1196. године и добила монашко име Анастасија“ — she was clothed as a nun in 1196 and received the monastic name Anastasia. That is the year of a tonsure. The corpus has no field for one, it is not a birth and not a death, and it is written in no field. This folder now holds a `death` and still lacks a `birth`, so `date-audit` will read its life for a birth: the paragraph carries 1196 **beside a clothing verb and no birth verb anywhere**, which is the standing rule about `stated` applied deliberately, and `stated` was measured before and after the commit to check it. **THE TWO NAMES, AND WHY ONLY ONE IS STORED.** „Њено крштено име је Ана“ — her baptismal name was Ana, Anastasia being the name she received at her tonsure. §6 is one form per folder, the fullest the calendar gives, and the heading gives Анастасија; **«Ана» is measured and not written**. `foldchk.py` returns `anna-of-larissa` and `anna-the-righteous`, both `sr`, for it — and `corpus-gate.mjs` prints **no `? "ана"` row at all**, which is the discrepancy the standing rule names: `foldchk.py` answers about the exact string and the gate about its own fold, and neither answer is reported as the other’s. Writing the baptismal name would have made a third holder of a string the gate does not watch, for no gain. **THE FAMILY, AND THE ONE ROW REFUSED IN IT.** „Супруга Стефана Немање. Мајка Вукана, Стефана и Растка“ — wife of Stefan Nemanja, mother of Vukan, Stefan and Rastko. Two of those the folder already relates: `simeon-the-myrrh-streaming` is Nemanja and `sava-of-serbia` is Rastko, both rows standing untouched and both confirmed by this book. **`stefan-the-first-crowned` exists and takes no row.** The heading and body give the son a bare «Стефан» with no epithet, and an identification made off a bare forename is not an identification, however short the list of candidates; the folder would also be reached through a genealogy the corpus already holds rather than through anything this book says. **It is the author’s to add**, and if it is added the reciprocal belongs with it. The name is written here and **not in the prose**, «Stefan the First-Crowned» being that folder’s display name and §6’s trap a display-name match. Vukan takes no row either: no folder holds him, and `david-son-of-vukan` is his son and not him, so a row there would be a kinship invented one generation out. `types` UNTOUCHED. Преподобна is the rank and gives the `venerable` the folder already carries off saint.gr’s Ὁσία; „мајка Светог Саве“ in the heading is a description and not a rank, and §6 keeps it out of the stored form as well. No `office` — a grand prince’s wife is not a see, and no pack holds a phrase for it; her husband’s rank is not hers. NO `locations`, AND THE RELICS ARE WHY IT IS WORTH SAYING. „Сахрањена је у припрати манастира Студенице. Њене мошти почивају у манастиру Студеници“ — buried in the narthex of the monastery of Studenica, and her relics rest there. That is a place named twice in two clauses and it is still not a coordinate; the folder has no `locations` and gains none. AND ONE SENTENCE THAT IS ABOUT THE PRESENT. „Пре неколико година ђакон Војислав Билбија је израдио диван саркофаг у коме се сада налазе њене мошти“ — some years ago the deacon Vojislav Bilbija made the fine sarcophagus her relics now lie in. **He takes no row and no folder**: a living or recent craftsman is not a companion, `ls saints | grep -i bilbij` holds nobody, and «неколико година» is not a date. It is written into the life because the book writes it, and it is the second time in two days that this source has named a named modern layman beside a saint’s relics, after the two brothers of Resen on 20 June. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the day carries only the verse. THE VERSE IS NOT USED, AND ON THIS DAY THAT COSTS SOMETHING. The ПЕСМА for 21 June is the longest of the wave so far and it tells a scene the prose entry does not: Julian building a tomb for his brother Julius beside their ninety-ninth church, Julius telling him mildly to prepare himself, for the grave is built for him and he will go before his brother, and God appointing Julius to build the hundredth church on a lonely island. **It is Bishop Nikolai’s own verse and not the entry’s account**, and §3 of this wave’s brief puts the verse in no field and in no life; so the scene is recorded here, where a reading belongs, and written into neither paragraph. THE DAY’S THIRD ENTRY IS REFUSED FOR WANT OF A FOLDER, AND THE CORPUS HAS ALREADY REFUSED THIS MAN ONCE. „Свети мученик Арчил II, цар грузињски“ — Archil II, king of Georgia, son of king Stephen and grandson of the great Georgian king Vakhtang, a great Christian and a protector of Christianity, tortured by the Muslims and beheaded for Christ on 20 March 744, being eighty years old when he suffered. `ls saints | grep -iE 'archil|luarsab'` returns nobody and `grep -ril Archil saints/*/saint.json` returns exactly one folder: `six-thousand-martyrs-of-david-gareji`, whose own attestation note already says that «the **king Archil of Georgia** gathered all the martyrs’ relics and buried them honourably» and that **«Arsenius and Archil are named as the entry names them and identified with nobody»**. So this is not a reader’s first refusal of Archil but the corpus’s second, and the two agree: he is named and he gets no folder. Ruling 3, therefore — and **20 March 744, the eighty years and the lineage are written nowhere**, the eighty years being a lifespan besides. `vakhtang-gorgasali` exists and takes no row and no mention in any prose written today: a grandfather is a kinship, but there is no grandson’s folder for it to be a kinship on. THE DAY’S FOURTH ENTRY IS REFUSED FOR WANT OF A FOLDER. „Свети мученик Луарсаб II, књаз карталински у Грузији“ — Luarsab II, prince of Kartli in Georgia, whose father George X also suffered for the faith and was poisoned by the Persian shah; thrown into a prison near Shiraz where he lay seven years, and then by the order of shah Abbas I hanged in the prison together with two servants, on 21 June 1622, with a heavenly light seen over his grave. `ls saints | grep -i luarsab` returns nobody, and `grep -ril Luarsab saints/*/saint.json` returns nobody either; `grep -ril Kartli` holds four Georgian folders and none of them is he. Ruling 3: named here, left out of every life written today, no folder from me, and **1622, the seven years, George X, Abbas I and the two servants are written nowhere**. The two servants are a narrated martyrdom with no name, which takes no row and no folder on the settled rule.

death.note: The Охридски пролог for 21. јун ст. ст.: „Упокојила се 21. јуна 1200. године“ — she reposed on 21 June 1200. The folder held no `dates` at all before this, saint.gr’s account being one sentence naming her the mother of Sava and a disclaimer that it has no other details of her life, with no year and no century. The same page gives the year of her tonsure, 1196, which is the year of a tonsure and not of a birth or a death and is written in no field; and the day in the sentence above is the day of the feast this row carries, which is recorded as an agreement and is not what the feast was read off (5 October 2026).
